hero.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher su.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for social media comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended after posting comments on Facebook that labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made "numerous findings" that "are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that his removal was appropriate.

Judge Livingstone issued an order last month recommending Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. She cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald returns to his position, with no announced timeline for a decision.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lt. Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Two former press secretaries to Gov.
cards.body:
Two former press secretaries to Gov. Ron DeSantis have accused Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, of operating anonymous social media accounts that promoted her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking the Governor. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, cited online research by Promota CEO Robert Salvador linking the X account @FSUdude01670 to a phone number and email address matching Layla Collins' known contact information. Florida Politics obtained screenshots showing that a two-factor authentication attempt on the account triggered a message to an email address and phone number with identifying digits matching those associated with Layla Collins. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins based on similar connection patterns.

Both accounts were deactivated shortly after Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public. Pushaw noted the accounts exclusively posted content promoting Jay Collins and attacking those who did not endorse him, including DeSantis. Redfern confirmed the technical connection, stating the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Pushaw questioned why a member of a state board appointed by DeSantis would maintain accounts calling the Governor a coward. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. DeSantis faces term limits and cannot seek a third term but has declined to endorse any candidate in the race to succeed him. Florida Politics requested comments from both Jay and Layla Collins but has not received responses.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for Fourth of July boaters with two boats on standby
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit the waterways across Florida this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is preparing for the surge in holiday boaters by positioning two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters launching from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety as they head out for the holiday weekend. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan for Tropicana Field redevelopment
cards.teaser: The Burg Bid proposal includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units, a 13-acre civic park, and a permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida on 58 acres of city-owned land.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred redevelopment plan for Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal centers on transforming stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, and entertainment venues. The developers would purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be required when the purchase and sale agreement is executed.

Unlike previous redevelopment proposals built around a new stadium, The Burg Bid organizes the district around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space within 18.5 acres of total public park area. The park would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, and a concert lawn. The Woodson museum would serve as an anchor for the district, positioned along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link that connects City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. The plan also includes a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal transportation hub, workforce and small-business center, and Resilience Event Center. CEO Thompson Whitney Blake noted in the proposal that the team designed "an evocative, architecturally jaw dropping permanent home for the Woodson African American Museum of Florida" and created the Legacy Link "that connects City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District."

The proposal heavily emphasizes the history of the former Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago to build Tropicana Field. The plan preserves the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and incorporates historic references throughout the Legacy Link. Nine bridges are planned over Booker Creek, echoing the nine bridges that once stood in the historic Gas Plant area. The proposal also calls for restoring Booker Creek itself, which had been reduced to a drainage ditch between parking lots.

The plan includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. Blue Sky Communities serves as the affordable housing partner. The development would occur in three phases of approximately five years each, with early construction potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors, Phase 2 would develop the mixed-income neighborhood, and Phase 3 would complete the district. The Rays' lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy medics for Fourth of July boating surge
cards.body:
As the Fourth of July weekend began, hundreds of boaters launched into Martin County waterways, prompting local maritime response teams to gear up for the holiday surge. Lt. Brett Harry with the Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team would position two boats with medics on standby across the county, with one unit covering the north section and another handling the south. The unit anticipates a busy weekend as residents take to the water to celebrate.

The maritime response teams are prepared to handle a wide range of emergencies that may occur on the water. According to Lt. Harry, their scope includes everything from minor incidents like stubbed toes to more serious medical events such as cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries. The teams will patrol Martin County waters throughout the holiday weekend to assist any boaters in distress or need of emergency response.

Among those heading out on the water Friday was the Shannon family, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. Brendan and Ashley Shannon emphasized that safety remains their top priority when boating. Their approach reflects the kind of responsible preparation that Lt. Harry encourages all boaters to practice during busy holiday weekends.

Lt. Harry stressed several critical safety measures for anyone planning to boat during the Fourth of July celebrations. He urged boaters to keep their focus on the water at all times and to designate a sober driver before launching. Additionally, he recommended that all boats be equipped with life vests, whistles and other flotation devices. By taking these precautions and following basic safety guidelines, boaters can help ensure a safe and enjoyable holiday weekend on Martin County waterways. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said, capturing the message that emergency responders want residents to remember as they celebrate on the water.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver recovered near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: Deputies recovered the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet, according to deputies. The recovery took place Friday near the inlet area.

Deputies reported finding the body after the diver was reported missing. The incident occurred in waters off Fort Pierce Inlet, a popular area for diving and boating activities.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the diver's death. The identity of the diver has not been released pending notification of family members.

hero.headline: Juno Beach debates replacing fence at JB-7 beach access as residents report trespassing
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers are cutting through private property since the town removed a fence at the JB-7 public walkway in 2023. The Juno Beach Town Council will address the fence question during budget discussions on July 15.
hero.body:
Residents at Colony Condos say the removal of a fence at the JB-7 public beach walkway has created a trespassing problem on their private property. The town took down the fence in 2023 for safety reasons, leaving only bushes to mark the boundary between the public access path and the condo's private land. Since then, residents have reported increased foot and vehicle traffic crossing onto their property during peak summer months.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described the scope of the problem. She said cars frequently park in private parking spots and beachgoers push through the landscaping with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs to access the beach. Hill explained that residents previously tried confronting trespassers directly but found people became hostile in response. Now they call police to handle the situation. She said the fence previously made the property boundary clear and helped prevent these incidents. Residents are hoping the town will reinstall it so they can reclaim their landscaping and parking areas.

The issue was brought before the Juno Beach Town Council, where officials acknowledged the town has no legal obligation to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable options. She proposed investigating whether the town could help pay for a lower-cost solution, such as a split rail fence combined with shrubs. The council agreed to discuss the fence question during its budget deliberations scheduled for July 15.

Not all beachgoers perceive the situation as problematic. Michael House, a regular beachgoer who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot blocks away, said he has not witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe. He noted that free parking is available and suggested that property damage and littering might be greater concerns than unauthorized foot traffic. His perspective highlights the different experiences residents and visitors have regarding the access point and its impact on the surrounding area.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida community selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the recognition reflects years of work focused on revitalizing the city and improving quality of life for residents. "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars," Lawson said.

The city's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of the community. She noted that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. The district also achieved a record 93.5 percent graduation rate.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, received an "A" or "B" rating, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record 93.5 percent graduation rate. District leaders reported that 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach emerged as a major success story, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years following five years as assistant principal, said staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program three years ago to take a closer look at student learning. Three other district schools also improved from a "C" to an "A" rating this year: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, received a denial from Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before her scheduled breast reconstruction surgery. The insurance company denied coverage for the GalaFlex mesh procedure, calling it investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, a 48-year-old breast cancer patient, received a denial from Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before her scheduled breast reconstruction surgery. Clark was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a synthetic surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational and there is no or not enough proof it improves health. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, worked to find a mechanism to make it happen. Billington uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes it is less risky than other options with proven success. An Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and that the GalaFlex mesh is not FDA-approved for breast reconstruction surgery and does not currently meet the standards required for coverage. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4. The band will represent the entire state of Florida at the prestigious event.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students heading into the national spotlight. "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well," she said. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, noting it demonstrates the program's growth. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing before millions of viewers but expressed belief the band will succeed. Senior Stephin Restivo emphasized the team's focus on marching precision and timing. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4 percent this year, survey finds
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5 percent and buns are up 7.7 percent.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The survey attributes the increase to inflation, with several cookout staples seeing significant price jumps. Ground beef prices are up 5.5 percent, buns are up 7.7 percent, strawberries are up 12.4 percent due to a Florida frost, and ice cream is up 5.3 percent.

Not all menu items have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals for groceries on your list and cutting down food waste by starting with a meal plan.

hero.headline: Juno Beach condo residents want fence restored at JB-7 beach access after trespassing complaints
hero.teaser: A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, and a fix could cost the town thousands of dollars.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos are seeking the restoration of a fence at the JB-7 public beach access point after complaining about trespassing and property damage since the town removed the barrier in 2023 for safety reasons. With only vegetation now separating the public walkway from private property, residents say beachgoers are increasingly cutting through their land and parking illegally. The dispute has escalated tensions between summer visitors and condo owners, prompting the town council to consider the matter during upcoming budget discussions.

Colony resident Lori Hill described how the problem intensifies during peak summer months. She said numerous vehicles park randomly in private spots, and people push through bushes to access the beach with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Before the fence was removed, Hill explained, the boundary between public and private property was clearly marked. Now without that visual barrier, confrontations between residents and trespassers have become frequent. Rather than engaging directly with intruders, residents have taken to calling police to handle the situations. Hill expressed hope that the town would reinstall the fence to restore order and protect their landscaping and private parking areas.

Not all beachgoers view the situation as problematic. Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not observed the trespassing issues residents describe. He noted that free parking is available in the area and suggested that property damage and littering might be separate concerns worth addressing. His perspective contrasts with the residents' account of regular boundary violations.

At a recent town council meeting, a municipal official clarified that the town has no legal obligation to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable alternatives. He proposed that the town might assist the condo association with a lower-cost fence option or a combination approach using split rail fencing mixed with shrubs. The council decided to formally address the fence question during its budget meeting scheduled for July 15, leaving the resolution uncertain as residents wait for action from town officials.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance in a deadly home fire earlier this week, with preliminary findings pointing to an electrical issue.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help her fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn reflected on her friendship with White and how she wants her to be remembered. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand." The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday is July 4, meaning she passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for controversial Fa.

The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no clear timeline for a final decision.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange for Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years, Samples said.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding the partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Glydways proposes elevated autonomous transit connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway above existing roads. The company describes the concept as a "horizontal elevator" that bypasses traffic congestion entirely. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center, potentially cutting the downtown-to-airport trip to less than 10 minutes.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned for the system because major transportation hubs already exist close together but are not easily connected. He pointed to increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road as evidence the region needs new transportation solutions. While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system, referencing previous South Florida estimates of 400 million to 500 million dollars per mile. Tuesday's meeting is not expected to approve construction but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has been selected as one of just 10 communities across the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city honored this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring together residents, local government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and create meaningful change. City leaders presented Riviera Beach's civic engagement efforts during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where the selection was announced.

Mayor Douglas Lawson described the recognition as a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He explained that the city earned the award through sustained efforts to revitalize Riviera Beach and enhance quality of life for residents. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said. City leaders emphasized that the honor reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and government, and creating opportunities for the community to participate directly in shaping the city's future.

Riviera Beach's application showcased several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment. The Riviera Beach Youth Council helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, while the Citizens Leadership Academy provides civic education with a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson highlighted the broader commitment behind these initiatives, stating "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city." She credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. Being named an All-America City signals to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and residents remain deeply engaged in shaping their community's future. City officials say the designation celebrates the city's progress while positioning it for future opportunities and continued growth. The other nine cities receiving the award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.
