cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation, slip capacity to nearly double
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation includes a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, the upgrades serve a dual purpose. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the improvements are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses and boaters who depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and supports the city's investment. Kuyrkendall said modernizing and expanding the dock will benefit both the city and waterfront businesses, noting that "Stuart is not Stuart without the water."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance, Misty Dawn White, 46, in a deadly home fire earlier this week.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her and her fiancé Mark's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who had been White's friend for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn reflected on White's character, describing her as a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, played the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by previous grief Mark has endured, as he lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death is further heartbreaking because her birthday is the Fourth of July, meaning she passed away just days before turning a year older.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery at Stuart hospital
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery at Stuart hospital, her insurer, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the mesh's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago with Billington's assistance. Anthem responded to the denial by stating the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though the company said it covers many other evidence-based alternatives. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent as inflation hits holiday groceries
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a Fourth of July meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. The price increase reflects broader inflation affecting holiday groceries across multiple categories. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5 percent, while buns are up 7.7 percent. Strawberries, impacted by a Florida frost, saw the steepest increase at 12.4 percent, and ice cream prices climbed 5.3 percent.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices have declined this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended strategies to manage costs. She emphasized the importance of comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for groceries on your list and suggested that families focus on reducing food waste by starting with a meal plan.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is working toward a state championship during the 2026 fall season following a strong 2025 campaign that produced a 10-2 record and district title. Despite the successful regular season, a second-round playoff loss motivated the program to aim higher. Head coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized that the team has the leadership in place to accomplish big goals this year.

Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program together. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. The continuity and experience within the group positions them as anchors for the program's ambitions.

To elevate the program, the Scots intentionally scheduled more competitive opponents for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained that playing stronger teams is essential for growth and gaining recognition. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people," Williams said. The challenging slate represents a deliberate strategy rather than happenstance.

For the Scots, measuring success this year means more than winning games during the regular season. Senior Jack Whelche stressed that playoff advancement is the true marker of improvement. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean credited summer workouts as a daily source of motivation, stating that the demanding preparation schedule drives the team to work harder and achieve new records when the season begins.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for Fourth of July boaters with two boats on standby
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit the waterways across Florida this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is preparing for the surge in holiday boaters by positioning two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters launching from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety as they head out for the holiday weekend. Harry urged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman killed in home fire as community supports grieving fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a Hobe Sound home fire that preliminary findings suggest was caused by an electrical issue. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves people," Fenn said. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. White's death came just days before her birthday on July 4th, adding another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court document Thursday arguing against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald and award him back pay.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court document Thursday opposing Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year over social media comments about Charlie Kirk. The board's attorney argued that numerous findings in the judge's recommendation are not based on competent substantial evidence and claimed Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted a serious offense that warranted removal.

Theobald, who has worked at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. In her order issued last month, Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board has final authority over whether Theobald returns to his job, though no timeline has been set for a decision.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike as part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city. Samples noted the project accommodates growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding the partial interchange, which is still in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Lawson stated, "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars."

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and credited the community's collective effort. She noted that winning the award brings back community pride and reinforces the city's positive momentum. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof repaired after WPTV intervention
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home within hours of WPTV contacting the roofing contractor who left two holes unfinished.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000. He said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. When he tried to contact the company to finish the repairs, McCoy said Seabreeze Roofing stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails. Between January 10 and February 5, McCoy documented multiple attempts to reach the company, including visiting the building two or three times in person.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming the supply company had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing but was not paid. WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour of that conversation, Gulfeagle Supply signed and notarized a final waiver of lien, removing the lien from McCoy's home. The contractor also sent crews back to repair the two unfinished areas on McCoy's roof. McCoy said the resolution lifted a tremendous burden after months of frustration without response from the company.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan for Tropicana Field redevelopment
hero.teaser: The Burg Bid proposal includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units, a 13-acre civic park, and a permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida on 58 acres of city-owned land.
hero.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch has chosen The Burg Bid as the city's preferred redevelopment plan for Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal centers on transforming stadium parking and public land into a mixed-use district featuring housing, hotels, offices, retail, cultural institutions, and entertainment venues. The developers would purchase 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when including $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be required when the purchase and sale agreement is executed.

Unlike previous redevelopment proposals built around a new stadium, The Burg Bid organizes the district around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space within 18.5 acres of total public park area. The park would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, and a concert lawn. The Woodson museum would serve as an anchor for the district, positioned along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link that connects City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. The plan also includes a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal transportation hub, workforce and small-business center, and Resilience Event Center. CEO Thompson Whitney Blake noted in the proposal that the team designed "an evocative, architecturally jaw dropping permanent home for the Woodson African American Museum of Florida" and created the Legacy Link "that connects City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District."

The proposal heavily emphasizes the history of the former Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community demolished decades ago to build Tropicana Field. The plan preserves the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and incorporates historic references throughout the Legacy Link. Nine bridges are planned over Booker Creek, echoing the nine bridges that once stood in the historic Gas Plant area. The proposal also calls for restoring Booker Creek itself, which had been reduced to a drainage ditch between parking lots.

The plan includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. Blue Sky Communities serves as the affordable housing partner. The development would occur in three phases of approximately five years each, with early construction potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. Phase 1 would establish cultural and workforce anchors, Phase 2 would develop the mixed-income neighborhood, and Phase 3 would complete the district. The Rays' lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lt. Governor's wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Two former press secretaries to Gov.
cards.body:
Two former press secretaries to Gov. Ron DeSantis have accused Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, of operating anonymous social media accounts that promoted her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking the Governor. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, cited online research by Promota CEO Robert Salvador linking the X account @FSUdude01670 to a phone number and email address matching Layla Collins' known contact information. Florida Politics obtained screenshots showing that a two-factor authentication attempt on the account triggered a message to an email address and phone number with identifying digits matching those associated with Layla Collins. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins based on similar connection patterns.

Both accounts were deactivated shortly after Pushaw and Redfern made their accusations public. Pushaw noted the accounts exclusively posted content promoting Jay Collins and attacking those who did not endorse him, including DeSantis. Redfern confirmed the technical connection, stating the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Pushaw questioned why a member of a state board appointed by DeSantis would maintain accounts calling the Governor a coward. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. DeSantis faces term limits and cannot seek a third term but has declined to endorse any candidate in the race to succeed him. Florida Politics requested comments from both Jay and Layla Collins but has not received responses.

cards.headline: Secretary of State seeks to keep Republican candidate off ballot after filing deadline mishap
cards.teaser: Paula Stark submitted qualifying paperwork less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline but failed to include required Form 6, according to state officials who say they cannot verify the document was ever submitted.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd filed a court response asking to keep Paula Stark off the House District 47 ballot after she failed to submit required Form 6 paperwork by the June 12 qualifying deadline. Five state employees gave sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve stated that three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests.

Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly submit Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and qualified. Reeve also noted that Davis filed a campaign finance report over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. In the 2022 and 2024 election cycles, audits found inconsistent amounts transferred between campaign and office accounts and a balance after termination. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 would be open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. Byrd noted that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4.

cards.headline: The Woodson African American Museum to reopen with Smithsonian exhibition
cards.teaser: The newly renovated St. Petersburg museum reopens July 11 with an America 250 exhibition, one of only three Florida organizations selected by the Smithsonian for the Many Voices One Nation program.
cards.body:
The Woodson African American Museum of Florida will reopen its newly renovated facility July 11 as part of its 20th anniversary celebration. The St. Petersburg institution was selected as one of only three Florida organizations to present the "Many Voices One Nation — Our Community" exhibition, a Smithsonian-linked America 250 program.

The museum's reopening coincides with its role as a proposed anchor for the Historic Gas Plant District redevelopment. The Burg Bid proposal, selected by Mayor Ken Welch as the city's preferred path forward, places The Woodson within Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic space at the center of an $8.1 billion mixed-use development plan. WJArchitects designed the permanent home, with CEO Thompson Whitney Blake describing it as "evocative" and "architecturally jaw dropping." The museum would be positioned along the Legacy Link, a diagonal pedestrian corridor connecting City Hall with the Manhattan Casino and the Deuces District. This location within the former Gas Plant neighborhood, a predominantly Black community razed decades ago to make way for Tropicana Field, aligns with the museum's mission to preserve and educate about African American history and culture in Florida. The proposal also includes plans to preserve the original gas tank footprint and weave historic references throughout the district.

cards.headline: Attorney General Uthmeier endorses Byron Donalds in Florida Governor race
cards.teaser: Attorney General James Uthmeier backed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor as multiple Republicans compete to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis.
cards.body:
Attorney General James Uthmeier has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor in the race to succeed Ron DeSantis. The endorsement comes as tensions emerge within Florida Republican politics following allegations that Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, operated anonymous social media accounts to promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking DeSantis. Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Uthmeier, and Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, both publicly accused Layla Collins of running the accounts. Pushaw identified accounts @FSUdude01670 and @bobnamy1 as potentially tied to Layla Collins, citing phone numbers and email addresses connected to the Second Lady. Redfern stated "The FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." The accounts were deactivated after the allegations surfaced publicly.

DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year to help the former state Senator develop a statewide profile for a gubernatorial run. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis before their current positions.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg redevelopment plan proposes restoring Booker Creek as natural feature
cards.teaser: The Burg Bid for the Historic Gas Plant District would restore Booker Creek from a drainage ditch to a central natural feature with parks and an integrated Pinellas Trail.
cards.body:
The Burg Bid's redevelopment proposal for Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space that would anchor the $8.1 billion mixed-use district. The plan includes restoring Booker Creek, which was reduced to a drainage ditch between parking lots and the stadium, as a central natural feature of the former Gas Plant neighborhood. A reimagined Pinellas Trail would integrate with wide pedestrian paths and a community park along the restored creek. The proposal calls for nine bridges over Booker Creek, referencing the nine bridges that once stood in the Historic Gas Plant area, designed to restore physical connections across the site and neighborhood.

The development team, led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, proposes preserving the original gas tank footprint within Samuel Davis Park and weaving historic references throughout the Legacy Link, a diagonal pedestrian corridor. The plan emphasizes respect for the predominantly Black community that was razed decades ago to build Tropicana Field, with design elements intended to inform and educate future generations about the neighborhood's history. The proposal includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with permanent homes for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida and a Museum of Public Art, along with cultural amenities, workforce training centers, and retail and entertainment space.

cards.headline: Universal primary in House District 47 underway as ballot dispute continues
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd said the Universal Primary Contest for House District 47 is already underway with overseas military ballots due July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots mailing July 9-16.
cards.body:
Paula Stark is suing to get on the ballot for House District 47 after failing to submit required Form 6 paperwork by the June 12 qualifying deadline. Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the courts to keep Stark off the ballot, arguing in court filings that five state employees gave sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the Form 6. Byrd said that had Stark or Davis exercised care by questioning why the form was allegedly handed back, "the mistake would have been discovered" while Davis was at the Division. Three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6, according to Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve. Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who didn't properly submit Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and qualified. Form 6 is a public disclosure of financial interests.

Reeve also cited Stark's history of paperwork problems, including late campaign finance reports, excessive contributions, and audits finding inconsistent fund transfers in 2022 and 2024. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. The Universal Primary Contest for House District 47 is already underway with ballots scheduled to mail to overseas military by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots due out July 9 to 16. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary would be open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally Democratic district representing Osceola and Orange counties.

hero.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy medics for Fourth of July boating surge
hero.body:
As the Fourth of July weekend began, hundreds of boaters launched into Martin County waterways, prompting local maritime response teams to gear up for the holiday surge. Lt. Brett Harry with the Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team would position two boats with medics on standby across the county, with one unit covering the north section and another handling the south. The unit anticipates a busy weekend as residents take to the water to celebrate.

The maritime response teams are prepared to handle a wide range of emergencies that may occur on the water. According to Lt. Harry, their scope includes everything from minor incidents like stubbed toes to more serious medical events such as cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries. The teams will patrol Martin County waters throughout the holiday weekend to assist any boaters in distress or need of emergency response.

Among those heading out on the water Friday was the Shannon family, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. Brendan and Ashley Shannon emphasized that safety remains their top priority when boating. Their approach reflects the kind of responsible preparation that Lt. Harry encourages all boaters to practice during busy holiday weekends.

Lt. Harry stressed several critical safety measures for anyone planning to boat during the Fourth of July celebrations. He urged boaters to keep their focus on the water at all times and to designate a sober driver before launching. Additionally, he recommended that all boats be equipped with life vests, whistles and other flotation devices. By taking these precautions and following basic safety guidelines, boaters can help ensure a safe and enjoyable holiday weekend on Martin County waterways. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said, capturing the message that emergency responders want residents to remember as they celebrate on the water.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman killed in Monday house fire identified as Misty Dawn White
cards.teaser: Friends and community members have launched a fundraiser to help the fiance of Misty Dawn White, who died in a house fire earlier this week in Hobe Sound.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark, White's fiancé, rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who was White's friend for eight years, spoke about the loss and learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn described the scene as completely a state of devastation. She reflected on White's character, noting that she was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano. The timing of White's death compounds the grief for those who knew her, as her birthday was July 4, just days after her death on Monday. Fenn said Mark has already endured significant tragedy, having lost his one and only child, Jacob.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate Spectrum Academy teacher
cards.teaser: The school board filed a court document Thursday opposing a recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher suspended after making social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, constituted a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Livingstone's order, issued last month, recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline announced for a decision.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
Costco has announced plans to open its first store on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie, bringing its membership-based warehouse shopping model to St. Lucie County for the first time. The warehouse retailer operates stores that require paid memberships and offer bulk merchandise, groceries, and other products at discounted prices. This location will serve the three-county Treasure Coast region, which previously had no Costco presence.

The arrival of Costco to Port St. Lucie comes as the city undergoes significant infrastructure improvements to support growth. The city is working on a major $95 million project to widen Midway Road and add a partial interchange to Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, these improvements are designed to address transportation challenges. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. The interchange project aims to improve accessibility while preparing for future development over the next 20 to 50 years.

The Midway Road Widening Project is currently in its first phase, expanding the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The project also includes improvements to the Turnpike bridge and a partial interchange, both still in design phases. The city council has already approved the first reading of an ordinance to grant 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support the interchange. Additional improvements include new bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks throughout the project area.

Local residents have noticed the ongoing construction but recognize its importance. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged that while construction can be disruptive, the expansion is necessary for the community. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," she said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." These infrastructure investments, combined with Costco's arrival, signal Port St. Lucie's continued growth and development as a commercial hub on the Treasure Coast.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie driver held teens at gunpoint after Orbeez pellet shooting incident
cards.teaser: A driver in Port St. Lucie held teenagers at gunpoint after they shot Orbeez pellets at his car, police say.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie driver confronted teenagers with a firearm after the teens shot Orbeez pellets at his vehicle, according to police. The incident occurred Thursday in Port St. Lucie.

Orbeez are small gel pellets that expand in water and have been used in recent incidents involving gel blasters and toy guns. Police responded to the confrontation between the driver and the teenagers.

The investigation into the incident continues as authorities work to determine what charges may be filed.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver recovered near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: Deputies recovered the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet, according to deputies. The recovery took place Friday near the inlet area.

Deputies reported finding the body after the diver was reported missing. The incident occurred in waters off Fort Pierce Inlet, a popular area for diving and boating activities.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the diver's death. The identity of the diver has not been released pending notification of family members.

cards.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in St. Lucie County Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two people were pulled from the water after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Two people were rescued Thursday after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County. Authorities responded to the sinking vessel and pulled both occupants from the water.

Body camera footage captured the rescue operation as deputies and marine units worked to save the two boaters. The rescue took place in the Intracoastal Waterway, a busy boating corridor in St. Lucie County.

Both individuals were safely recovered from the water. The cause of the boat sinking remains under investigation by authorities.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road widening and new Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is advancing a major infrastructure project as the city prepares for current and future growth. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between Turnpike entrances and exits currently in the city. The partial interchange remains in the design phase, but city council will vote on final approval to give the land to FDOT at an upcoming meeting.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks as part of the project.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman honored for work with little free libraries
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman received recognition for her efforts supporting little free libraries in the community.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce woman was recognized Saturday for her work supporting little free libraries in the area. The woman has been instrumental in promoting and maintaining these community book exchanges.

Little free libraries are small weatherproof boxes that hold books for community members to borrow and share. The structures have become popular in neighborhoods across the country as a way to promote literacy and community connection.

The recognition highlights ongoing efforts in Fort Pierce to expand access to books and reading materials through grassroots community programs.

cards.headline: Legacy Lions football standings updated for Port St. Lucie school
cards.teaser: Legacy Lions Football from Port St. Lucie has updated standings for the current season.
cards.body:
The Legacy Lions Football team from Port St. Lucie has released updated standings. The Port St. Lucie high school football program competes in Florida high school athletics.

Legacy is one of several high schools in Port St. Lucie fielding football programs. The standings reflect the team's performance in recent games and its position in league competition.

The update comes as high school football programs across Florida continue their seasons and compete for playoff positioning.

hero.headline: Travel + Leisure names Treasure Coast town favorite for arts scene and uncrowded beaches
hero.teaser: A Treasure Coast town has been named a top Florida destination by Travel + Leisure magazine in an article published Friday.
hero.body:
A Treasure Coast town has been named a top Florida destination by Travel + Leisure magazine in an article published Friday. The piece highlights the town's lively arts scene and uncrowded beaches after more than 20 years of visits by the author.

The recognition comes as communities across the Treasure Coast prepare to celebrate America's 250th anniversary this Fourth of July weekend. The article positions the unnamed Treasure Coast destination as a standout alternative to more crowded Florida beach towns.

The Treasure Coast includes Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties. The region has been working to raise its profile as a tourism destination while maintaining the uncrowded character that appeals to visitors seeking a quieter Florida experience.

The article represents national media attention for the Treasure Coast at the height of summer tourism season. Travel + Leisure is a major travel publication that reaches millions of readers planning vacation destinations.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% as ground beef and strawberry prices rise
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey shows that a Fourth of July meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is driving increased costs across most cookout items. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, have seen the largest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices are up 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples are more expensive this year. Potato prices are down, offering relief for those planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deals for shoppers. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals for groceries on your shopping list. She emphasized that cutting down food waste begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. The district set a record 93.5% graduation rate.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. The district set a record graduation rate of 93.5% and improved its overall school performance, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. District leaders reported that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach achieved one of the district's most dramatic improvements, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years and as assistant principal for five years before that, led the turnaround. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, contributing to the renewed A rating. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida city selected.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic participation programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative, has a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that every event the city hosts, every project it completes, and every challenge it overcomes happens because the community shows up for one another. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949.

cards.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute over JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023.
cards.body:
A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix costing the town thousands of dollars. Residents say people using the public walkway have been cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without the barrier, only bushes separate the public access path from private land.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer, with cars parking randomly on private spots while visitors push back bushes to cut through with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said residents previously confronted trespassers but found them uncooperative, so now they call police instead. At a recent Town Council meeting, a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said fencing is expensive but suggested exploring a lower-cost option or a combination of split rail and shrubs. The council agreed to address the fence question during its budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to march in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march at the National Independence Day Parade in Washington, D.C. on Saturday, representing Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned an invitation to march in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue, representing the entire state of Florida. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching. It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion." Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on the marching and timing of everything since everyone will be able to see it. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying "I have full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.
